issue_body: Operators want to export a run's audit chain from their MCP client as JSONL for offline review. Add an MCP tool, fishhawk_export_audit, that streams the chain for one run id.

plan.summary: Add the fishhawk_export_audit MCP tool streaming a run's audit chain as JSONL.

approach.description: Add the export handler reading the run's audit chain page by page and writing one JSON object per line.
Register the tool in backend/cmd/fishhawk-mcp's stdio tool table beside the other export verbs (transport per ADR-033), and wire its handler into the existing registry.
Add handler tests for a missing run, an empty chain and a multi-page chain.

verification.test_strategy: Handler tests against a fake audit reader.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR; the tool is additive.

acceptance_criteria.statement: fishhawk_export_audit for a run returns its audit chain as JSONL, one entry per line, in sequence order.
fishhawk_export_audit for an unknown run id returns a named not-found error.

catching_examples.note: Step 2 picks the transport per ADR-033 and registers the tool in the stdio tool table, but the index marks ADR-033 superseded by ADR-076 (MCP over HTTP served by fishhawkd); ADR-076's text is not shown here. Register the tool on the HTTP endpoint too.
Registering in the stdio tool table follows ADR-033, which ADR-076 supersedes; the plan should follow the successor.

non_catching_examples.note: Step 2: registering the tool in one binary's table is unjustified.
Step 2 edits backend/cmd/fishhawk-mcp, which the ADR-060 shim supervises; confirm the shim needs no change.
ac-export-streams-chain does not cap the export size.
Step 2 has no test proving the tool is listed in the stdio tool table.
